title: Boss: on call
summary: Turn raw cluster output into a triage report and check access.

steps.title: The scene
steps.body: It is 02:00 and the pager says *checkout errors*. You have `kubectl get pods` output and not much patience. Build the report you wish you had.

steps.title: Triage report
prompt: Write `List<string> Report(string output)` for `kubectl get pods` text (columns `NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE`, header first). For every pod that is not healthy (same rule as module 1: READY numbers differ or STATUS is not `Running`/`Completed`), return `"NAME: STATUS -> COMMAND"` with:
Order: most `RESTARTS` first (the RESTARTS column may look like `7` or `7 (2m ago)`: take the first number), then by name.
solution: var rows = new List<(string Name, string Status, int Restarts)>();
template: Dojo.Eq("all healthy", new List<string>(), Report("NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE\na 1/1 Running 0 1m"));
hints: After splitting on spaces, `7 (2m ago)` becomes several columns; column 3 is still the number.

steps.title: Why is it Pending?
prompt: Write `string WhyPending(int reqCpuM, int reqMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> nodeSelector, List<(string Name, int FreeCpuM, int FreeMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> Labels)> nodes)` that produces a message like the scheduler's:
`"0/N nodes are available: A Insufficient cpu, B Insufficient memory, C didn't match node selector."`

For each node check, in order: selector mismatch (count it in C and stop), then CPU (A) and memory (B), where a node can count in both. Leave out parts whose count is 0, keep the order cpu, memory, selector, join with `", "`, end with `.`. If some node fits, return `"schedulable on NAME"` (first such node).
starter: string WhyPending(int reqCpuM, int reqMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> nodeSelector,
List<(string Name, int FreeCpuM, int FreeMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> Labels)> nodes)
solution: string WhyPending(int reqCpuM, int reqMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> nodeSelector,
List<(string Name, int FreeCpuM, int FreeMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> Labels)> nodes)
if (!nodeSelector.All(kv => n.Labels.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var v) && v == kv.Value)) { sel++; continue; }
bool cpuOk = n.FreeCpuM >= reqCpuM, memOk = n.FreeMemMi >= reqMemMi;
if (sel > 0) parts.Add($"{sel} didn't match node selector");
template: var dojoNodes = new List<(string Name, int FreeCpuM, int FreeMemMi, Dictionary<string, string> Labels)> {
Dojo.Eq("cpu, memory and selector", "0/3 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu, 2 Insufficient memory, 1 didn't match node selector.",
Dojo.Eq("fits on gpu1 with no selector", "schedulable on gpu1", WhyPending(4000, 4096, new(), dojoNodes));
Dojo.Eq("fits on n2", "schedulable on n2", WhyPending(1000, 256, new(), dojoNodes));
Dojo.Eq("only selector", "0/3 nodes are available: 3 didn't match node selector.", WhyPending(1, 1, new() { ["pool"] = "arm" }, dojoNodes));
hints: Three counters; a selector mismatch skips the resource checks for that node.
Build a list of the non-zero parts and `string.Join` them.

steps.title: Who can break production?
prompt: Write `List<string> Dangerous(List<(string Subject, string Role, string Ns)> bindings)` that flags risky grants. A binding is dangerous when:
Return `"Subject: Role in Ns"` for each, sorted by subject (ordinal), and keep input order for the same subject.
starter: List<string> Dangerous(List<(string Subject, string Role, string Ns)> bindings)
solution: List<string> Dangerous(List<(string Subject, string Role, string Ns)> bindings)
template: var dojoB = new List<(string Subject, string Role, string Ns)> {
Dojo.Eq("flags", new List<string> { "group:platform: admin in *", "group:platform: cluster-admin in kube-system", "system:serviceaccount:ci:runner: cluster-admin in *" }, Dangerous(dojoB));
hints: `OrderBy` is stable, so equal subjects keep input order.
Write the condition exactly as the two bullets say.
